user.title: Blink Live View Proxy
user.description: Connect Home Assistant to the local Blink live-view proxy. Live-view duration controls how long the direct player asks the proxy to keep each stream open; Blink may still end a session early.

data_description.stream_seconds: Allowed range: 10-300 seconds. Longer sessions can use more Blink live-view quota and may run into camera or cloud-side limits.

proxy_outdated.title: The Blink proxy is older than this integration needs
proxy_outdated.description:
The proxy at {base_url} reports {proxy_version}. This integration needs {minimum_version} or newer.

Live view, clips and push-to-talk keep working. What fails is anything the newer proxy added — browser authentication answers 404, because those routes have never existed in that build.

The two halves update independently: HACS moves the integration, and nothing moves the proxy. On a Linux service install, run this on the proxy host from a checkout of the repository:

```
sudo scripts/install-proxy.sh
```

It keeps your token, config and Blink session, and restarts the service. Add-on installs update from the add-on store.

This notice clears itself once the proxy reports {minimum_version} or newer.

proxy_outdated_fixable.title: The Blink proxy is older than this integration needs

confirm.title: Update the Blink proxy
confirm.description:
The proxy at {base_url} reports {proxy_version}.

Home Assistant will ask it to run the updater it was installed with, which fetches the newest release and restarts the proxy. Any live view playing at that moment stops, and clips, tokens and your Blink session are kept.

For a systemd proxy, the dialog closes once the updater starts. For an add-on, it waits for Supervisor to finish the update. This notice clears itself within a minute or two after the proxy comes back and reports its new version.

abort.already_running: An update is already running on the proxy. Give it a minute, then check whether this notice has cleared on its own.
abort.not_supported: This proxy cannot update itself. Update it the way it was installed: re-run scripts/install-proxy.sh on the host, or pull the new image and recreate the container.
abort.no_addon: Supervisor does not list a Blink Live View Proxy add-on, so there is nothing here to update. Update it from Settings → Add-ons.
abort.entry_gone: This proxy is no longer set up in Home Assistant, so there is nothing left to update.
abort.update_failed: The proxy could not be asked to update. Check that it is reachable and that the token is still valid, then look at the proxy host's logs.
